requested.title: Background command guard can be bypassed through shell indirection

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: BackgroundJobs.start accepts the model-supplied command, calls checkCommand once, and then passes the unchanged string to repoBackgroundRunner. startBackground embeds that string in backgroundStartScript's inner body, which is executed by `sh -c`; therefore shell evaluation occurs after the textual inspection. checkCommand only tokenizes literal command segments and selectively recurses into literal shell `-c` arguments, so `eval 'git push origin HEAD'`, a variable-expanded command, or a sourced script has no top-level git invocation for it to reject. This limitation is explicitly acknowledged in command-guard.ts, which states that `g=git; $g reset --hard` passes because parsing is not a real shell parser. The bypass is reachable in production cloud runs: supervisor.ts exposes run_background through the local tool bridge when the normal tool set includes it, and the bridge invokes BackgroundJobs.handle. The cloud clone stores the VM-specific forge credential in remote.origin.url; execute.ts deliberately passes vmTarget.authUrl to cloneRepo, and network-policy.ts explicitly documents that the forge token remains readable in `.git/config` within the VM. The Vercel Sandbox network policy has a catch-all `"*": []`, so it permits general outbound traffic rather than restricting exfiltration destinations. Thus a repository prompt injection that causes the model to submit an indirect background command can bypass the intended push/destructive-command guard and can read and send the scoped ephemeral repository credential or repository data outward. Recent history does not show a fix: the current guard still contains the acknowledged textual-parser limitation, while existing tests cover direct commands and literal nested `bash -c` forms but not eval, variable expansion, or sourced/dynamic commands. The existing token is repository-scoped and ephemeral, which supports the reported HIGH severity rather than elevating it to a broader credential compromise.
